question: A main agent is coordinating exploration of a repository with over 50,000 files and needs a complete list of every test file before planning a coverage audit. Running the search directly would flood the main conversation with thousands of matched paths it will not need again. What best keeps the main agent's context focused on high-level coordination while still producing the list?
options: A) Ask the user to manually paste the list of test file paths into the conversation before continuing with the audit.
B) Read every file in the repository sequentially in the main agent to identify which ones are tests by inspecting their contents.
C) Run the search directly in the main agent and keep the entire raw output in the conversation in case it needs to be referenced again later.
D) Spawn a subagent to search for test files and return only the consolidated list, leaving the raw output isolated in its own context.
correct_answers: D) Spawn a subagent to search for test files and return only the consolidated list, leaving the raw output isolated in its own context.
explanations: Incorrect. Manually collecting the list defeats the purpose of using the agent for exploration and adds unnecessary user burden for a task the agent can perform directly.
Incorrect. Reading every file's contents sequentially in the main agent is far more expensive than a targeted search and consumes even more context than the raw search output would.
Incorrect. Keeping the full raw search output in the main conversation is exactly the pattern that floods the coordinating agent's context with data it will not use again.
Correct. Delegating the search isolates the verbose discovery output in the subagent's own context window; the main agent receives only the distilled list and keeps its context free for coordination.
